text:
Sebastian Aho now has more goals than anyone in Hurricanes history. His goal in the 7-4 win over Edmonton on Nov. 21 was No. 323, a franchise record, on a three-point night. It's a fitting marker for a player who has spent his whole career in Carolina and is wearing a Stanley Cup ring from last spring.

He's at 33 points in 24 games (13 goals, 20 assists), and Carolina controls 60.5% of 5v5 expected goals, the quality of chances, when he's on. Some of the scoring is running hot: 13 goals on 10.4 expected, shooting 20% against 14% last season, and the team has scored 6.2 more goals than its chances with him on the ice. That part tends to fade. The process underneath is the real thing. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 9.9 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 93rd percentile among forwards, and Evolving-Hockey ranked him 16th among 401 forwards in wins above replacement. He plays like Sidney Crosby by our similarity measure. Our numbers project about 95 points.
headline: Sebastian Aho stands alone in Hurricanes history
